Eufy Omni C28 Where to Buy: $799.99 $379.99 at Amazon $799.99 $379.99 at Best Buy $799.99 $379.99 at Eufy (with code WS24C28200NEW1) The Verge’s smart home reviewer Jennifer Pattison Tuohy named the Eufy Omni C28 one of her top picks after testing 16 robot vacuum mops . She thinks it’s a particularly great fit for apartments and smaller homes. It offers features typically found in pricier flagship models, including a multifunction dock that automatically washes the mop roller with hot water and dries it with hot air, yet it doesn’t take up too much space. The robot itself is also relatively narrow and maneuvers easily around furniture and into tight spaces. It boasts excellent navigation, and had no trouble climbing over the legs of Jen’s lounger, which have tripped up many of the more expensive models she’s tested. The Omni C28 also does a great job cleaning with its mops, particularly on hardwood floors. Surprisingly, it’s powerful enough to lift up dried oatmeal. Unlike most other robot vacuums Jen’s tested, this one lacks a camera, making it a good option if you’re concerned about privacy. That’s because microSD Express cards , while physically identical to ones you might have lying around, have faster read and write speeds. Thankfully, Samsung’s 256GB model has dropped to $44.99 at Amazon ahead of Black Friday, which is a few bucks off its usual price but still well below its $79.99 MSRP. Sandisk’s 256GB card, meanwhile, is available for $49.99 ($10 off Amazon’s typical list price) from Amazon and Sandisk , if you prefer one brand over the other for some reason. For those who don’t want to think about upgrading their Switch 2’s storage again, both brands’ 512GB microSD Express cards are selling for a fair $99.99 on Amazon . That gives you double the storage for roughly twice the price of a 256GB card, as it should be. Samsung P9 microSD Express Card Where to Buy: $79.99 $44.99 at Amazon (256GB) $149.99 $99.99 at Amazon (512GB) Sandisk microSD Express card Where to Buy: $166.99 $99.99 at Best Buy (512GB) $73.99 $49.99 at Amazon (256GB) $166.99 $98.99 at Amazon (512GB) I suspect the 256GB option will be enough for most Switch 2 players, unless you buy a lot of games. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is 24.9 gigabytes, for example. Other Nintendo-developed games tend to be similar in install size, though it’s all over the place for third-party game makers; Resident Evil Requiem (which also recently dropped to $39.99 on Amazon ) is relatively small at 28.7 gigs, while The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered is about 50.
